title: Hemisphere navigation pivots — slimline contextual rail & workspace handoff
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current console navigation mixes workspace context, cross-workspace routes, and deep-route state in the same left rail. This causes friction when users switch workspaces (loss of place), makes rollouts and cost dashboards hard to surface consistently, and bloats the rail options for cross-tenant admins.

Goal: Propose a lightweight, progressive navigation pattern ("hemisphere pivots") that separates workspace-level routing from global routes via a slim contextual rail. Preserve deep-route location on workspace switch where feasible, provide clear fallback routes, and expose rollout & cost surfaces as first-class, discoverable targets without increasing cognitive load.

Deliverables: low-fi wireframes, two Figma interactive prototypes (rail collapsed / rail expanded), a short motion spec for workspace handoff, annotated IA map, and a usability checklist to validate in the next design critique.

Success metrics: reduce workspace-switch bounce (users losing context) in our prototype test by 60% and decrease time-to-find Rollouts dashboard by 40% in task-based tests.
acceptance_criteria: Slimline contextual rail prototype that shows 3 states: collapsed (icons), expanded (labels), and handoff modal
Workspace switch preserves route when compatible; when not compatible, user is presented with an explicit 'handoff' landing with two clear options
Rollouts and Cost views are surfaced in a consistent global section and in-workspace shortcuts without duplicating primary navigation targets
Accessibility: keyboard nav, aria labels, and 4.5:1 contrast in collapsed and expanded states
Developer handoff doc with tokenized dimensions and motion timings plus a small QA checklist
decisions: Separate concerns: left rail will contain two zones — Global (top) for cross-workspace routes like Rollouts/Cost/Audit and Workspace (bottom) for workspace-scoped routes like Models, Endpoints, and Routes

Workspace switching will attempt to preserve the current route by mapping to a compatible route in the target workspace. If mapping fails, we show a 'handoff' modal with options: translate to closest route or open workspace home
Collapsed rail will default to icon-only, with a persistent contextual tooltip that shows route preview and workspace name on hover/focus
To maintain predictability, use conservative animation timings: 140ms ease-out for expand, 120ms ease-in for collapse, 220ms for handoff modal fade+slide
Rollouts and Cost will be linked from both Global and Workspace scopes using route aliases (no duplicated content; alias resolves to same backend route)
No RBAC changes in this design iteration; controls will respect existing role checks server-side
tradeoffs_and_risks: Preserving route across workspaces increases complexity in routing logic and requires ENG effort to build a route-mapping layer
Alias links for Rollouts/Cost mean tests must ensure metrics attribution remains correct (security and audit implications), so additional telemetry work is required
Collapsed rail sacrifices label discoverability; mitigation: persistent tooltips and a short onboarding tip on first login
Motion and handoff modals introduce extra surface area for keyboard users — accessibility testing is mandatory before rollout
implementation_notes: Work with ENG to surface route compatibility table (ENG-7182) — prototype uses a JSON mapping in the figma notes
Add console feature flag 'hemisphere_nav' for staged rollout and A/B testing
Small UX SDK changes required: expose current-route metadata to workspace switcher and enable an opt-in 'preserve_route' param
Provide tokens for rail width: collapsed: 56px, expanded: 240px; icon grid spacing: 12px center
Request runtime telemetry event: nav.handoff.{accepted|fallback|cancelled} with prior_route and target_workspace metadata
open_questions: How do we handle deep-route params that are totally incompatible (e.g., jobId in Models present in source workspace but not in target)?
Should billing-cost deep links open in a separate global context or within the target workspace's billing view by default?
Do we show workspace previews in the handoff modal (last activity snapshot) or keep it minimal to reduce load time?
